Both options are Gate-6-class architectural decisions, not a 30-min hack. **Next-agent task:** open a D.NN entry titled "Provider tier — pre-authenticated audit trail for probing detection" and decide between (a) and (b) based on whether enterprise CISO review demands the trail (most likely option (a) — separate table).

- **Phase 4a S11 — Playwright E2E infrastructure + middleware smoke landed (2026-05-25, branch `phase-4a-fe`).** Adds `@playwright/test`, `playwright.config.ts` (dev-server-driven, Chromium-only), an `e2e/` directory with its own tsconfig, the `pnpm test:e2e` + `test:e2e:install` scripts, and a CI job that installs the chromium binary + runs the suite. **Critical security fix uncovered by the suite:** the default Next.js middleware matcher (`'/((?!api|_next|_vercel|.*\\..*).*)'`) excludes ANY path containing a `.` (intended for static assets), which silently skipped the middleware for the JWT-shape `/sign/<jwt>` surface — `isLocaleAgnosticPublic` was dead code AND `/sign/header.payload` (a non-JWT shape with a dot) bypassed the auth gate entirely. **Fixed:** matcher now includes an explicit `/sign/:path*` entry so the public-sign route is genuinely gated by the middleware regex. Without Playwright we wouldn't have caught this — Vitest tested the regex in isolation, not the matcher composition. **Scope (lean):** the 4 working E2E tests cover the security-critical middleware assertions (malformed token → /he/login; 2-segment "fake JWT" → /he/login; valid JWT → no redirect; /he/login renders). Full UI flow E2E (canvas draw → submit → success) deferred — Playwright `page.route()` + dev-mode SSR hydration race needs a BE fixture or `next start` mode to be reliable. **Test deltas:** web vitest 243/243 (unchanged); Playwright 4/4 pass against the dev server (~30s incl. dev-server boot). lint+typecheck clean.
- **Phase 4a S10 — Public residents' signing surface (D.12 LAW, public) landed (2026-05-25, branch `phase-4a-fe`).** `/sign/<jwt>` lives OUTSIDE `[locale]` with its own minimal layout (Hebrew RTL hardcoded — residents always sign in Hebrew; URL is JWT-only with no locale prefix so SMS/WhatsApp links stay short). Middleware extended with a `PUBLIC_LOCALE_AGNOSTIC_REGEX` that pins the JWT shape (`/^\/sign\/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/`) and skips both the auth gate AND next-intl — defense in depth against `/sign/foo` slipping into the public surface. **Anti-enumeration UX:** every error from GET / POST collapses to a single "הקישור אינו תקף" stage so an attacker can't distinguish expired vs cancelled vs forged vs already-signed (mirrors the BE's generic 401 `invalid_token`). **Atomic single-use:** the BE `UPDATE WHERE jti AND status='pending'` is authoritative; the FE simply renders the `signedAt` confirmation on success. **SVG canvas** (`_signature-canvas.tsx`): native Pointer Events with `touch-action: none`, per-stroke `<path d="M…L…"/>`, 1.5px minimum delta filter — outputs a self-contained `<svg xmlns viewBox>` body that matches `PublicSignSubmitInput.signatureSvg` (50-262144 bytes, `/^<svg[\s\S]*<\/svg>$/i`); defensive `PublicSignSubmitInput.safeParse(...)` runs BEFORE the POST. **HTTP posture:** `credentials: 'omit'` on both GET + POST (no manager cookies sent over the public-link wire); `robots: noindex/nofollow/nocache/noimageindex` on the layout `<head>` (ISO A.13.2.1 / A.18.1.4 — the URL is a bearer credential and must NEVER be indexed). MSW handlers added for both endpoints (preview + submit) with the same JWT-shape gate. **Test deltas:** web 243/243 (+5 — `middleware.spec.ts` M11-M15 pinning the public-surface regex against shape variations: valid JWT bypasses auth, malformed shapes fall through, path-injection `/sign/<jwt>/extra` blocked). lint+typecheck clean across all 8 packages.
- **Phase 4a S9 — Signature Requests (D.12 Manager side) landed (2026-05-25, branch `phase-4a-fe`).** Manager flow: `POST /signature-requests` returns the row + a single-use `signUrl` (7d JWT bearer; the FE shows it ONCE with a copy-to-clipboard affordance + a "leaked? cancel + regenerate" warning — never persisted in TanStack cache, never on list/detail reads). `GET /signature-requests?status=...` for filtered list with keyset cursor; `GET /signature-requests/:id` for detail; `POST /signature-requests/:id/cancel` is idempotent on `cancelled` and 409 `signature_request_already_signed` on `signed` (wired to a HE/EN UX message). Adapter encodes the 3-state machine (pending/signed/cancelled) into HE/EN labels + 4-color palette + `isCancellable` (only `pending` AND `expiresAt > now`) + `isExpired` (pending-past-expiry; the BE's atomic single-use guard has already killed the token). Sidebar `signatureRequests` link enabled (6 enabled nav items now). MSW handlers added for all 4 manager endpoints; `SAMPLE_SIGNATURE_REQUESTS` covers one of each terminal state + a live pending row; `samples.spec.ts` extended to validate `SignatureRequestSchema` + `SignatureDeliveryReportSchema` PLUS an invariant that the wire shape never carries `jti` / `token` (D.12 security invariant). **Test deltas:** web 238/238 (+18 — `adapters/signature-request.spec.ts` 15 covering 3-state HE/EN + TERMINAL/CANCELLABLE sets + expired-pending edge case + signed-past-expiry forensic invariant; samples drift gate +3 incl. the no-jti / no-token guard). lint+typecheck clean across all 8 packages.
- **Phase 4a S8 — Imports Wizard (D.34) landed (2026-05-25, branch `phase-4a-fe`).** Three-phase upload flow: FE computes sha256 client-side → `POST /api/v1/imports` returns the row + a presigned PUT URL → XHR upload directly to R2 (XHR over fetch so we surface live upload progress events) → `POST /api/v1/imports/:id/start` enqueues the worker. Live progress is a same-origin `EventSource` on `/api/v1/imports/:id/stream` — every frame is `ImportSseEventSchema.parse(JSON.parse(line))` (discriminated union: `progress` | `end` | `gone`). Terminal frames close the stream AND invalidate the TanStack cache so the canonical row counters re-fetch. Adapter encodes the 8-state machine into Hebrew labels + 4-color palette + `isTerminal`/`isCancellable`/`isAwaitingMapping` booleans driving the UI. `awaiting_mapping` lights up a dedicated wizard at `/imports/:id/mapping` — 6 canonical fields (`national_id`/`name`/`phone`/`apartment_number`/`building_address`/`ownership_pct` — last optional), column-index inputs with duplicate detection + missing-field warning, optional template name; `SubmitMappingInput.safeParse(body)` runs defensively right before the POST. UX maps 6 error codes (`upload_failed`/`import_conflict`/`upload_size_mismatch`/`storage_unavailable`/`validation_error`/`wrong_file_type`) to localized messages. Sidebar `imports` link enabled. MSW handlers added for all 8 imports endpoints (list/get/create/start/mapping/cancel/errors/stream); `SAMPLE_IMPORTS` carries one of each interesting state (parsing/done/awaiting_mapping); `samples.spec.ts` schema-parse gate extended to cover `ImportJobSchema` + `ImportErrorSchema`. **Test deltas:** web 220/220 (+20 — `adapters/import.spec.ts` 16 covering 8-state HE/EN exhaustively + TERMINAL/CANCELLABLE sets + progressPct null/cap-100 invariants; samples drift gate +2; existing handler/route coverage exercised by isolation spec). lint+typecheck clean across all 8 packages.

- **v8.5 P0 cross-confirmed closures:**
  - **Migrator GUC fragility (SOLID #1 + Sec P0-1)** — `packages/db/scripts/migrate.ts` was setting `app.encryption_key` on a checked-out client then releasing it, relying on pg-pool LIFO so the migrator's next checkout would inherit the GUC. Own code documented this as "we can't rely 100% on this" — a P0 because race or driver-change could silently produce ciphertexts no one can ever decrypt. **Fix:** hold a dedicated client through the entire migrate() lifecycle, bind drizzle to it directly, verify GUCs took before running, fail-fast sentinel if `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` / `PII_HASH_KEY` is empty.
  - **SSE counter race (SOLID #3 + Sec HIGH-6)** — `ImportsController.activeStreams += 1` lived OUTSIDE the try/finally. Synchronous throw between increment and try-entry (writeHead on a closed socket) would leak the counter forever, monotonically drifting the pod's perceived stream count to `MAX_ACTIVE_STREAMS` and serving permanent 503 to all new SSE clients. **Fix:** increment FIRST (still inside the cap-check ⇒ no TOCTOU), then wrap everything else in the try/finally. The finally is now the only counter-touching path.
- **v8.5 P0 single-agent + concrete bug closures:**
  - **`cancel()` doesn't purge bytes (SOLID #4)** — Manager cancel path wrote `cancelled` to import_jobs but NEVER called the purge — worker only purges on terminal state via its own code path. PII bytes leaked FOREVER on the most common terminal route. **Fix:** lifted `purgeImportBytes` from `apps/worker` to `@emapp/db` (`packages/db/src/helpers/import-bytes.ts`), apps/worker now thin re-export, API `cancel()` calls it post-commit; added new `'purge-failed'` return code (was overloaded with `'not-terminal'`); dropped `r2_key_prefix` from audit metadata (was leaking orgId slice — Sec HIGH-5); `actorType:'system'` instead of crediting Manager (semantic cleanliness — SOLID #5).
  - **`withProvider` missing encryption GUCs (Sec P0-2)** — `packages/db/src/wrappers/with-provider.ts` set only `app.provider_user_id` + `app.access_reason`; any Provider Admin owner-read would throw on `current_setting('app.encryption_key')`. **Fix:** parameter-bound four-GUC set_config — adds `app.encryption_key` + `app.pii_hash_key`, mirroring withTenant.
  - **Sequential decrypts on critical path (Perf F1+F2)** — signature-requests `loadOwnerWithPii` did 3 sequential round-trips per send (SELECT → pgp_sym_decrypt name → pgp_sym_decrypt phone). 90–150 ms of pure pgcrypto latency on the Manager UX critical path. **Fix:** collapsed into a single SQL that returns both decrypted columns via `pgp_sym_decrypt(...)` + CASE WHEN for the optional phone. Net latency: ~30–50 ms.
- **v8.5 HIGH closures:**
  - **R2 delete blocks worker (Perf F4)** — `storage.delete` in `purgeImportBytes` had no deadline; an R2 outage pinned the worker slot for the S3 client's `socketTimeout` (30 s default), starving pg-boss concurrency. **Fix:** `Promise.race` against a 5-second deadline (`deleteTimeoutMs` configurable); on timeout returns `'purge-failed'` so future sweeper retries. Timer `.unref()`'d so it can't keep the event loop alive.
  - **audit_log cleartext owner name (SOLID #7)** — `owners.create()` wrote `afterState: { name: input.name }` to audit_log, defeating the v8-S3 owners.name encryption-at-rest. **Fix:** parity with `update()` — `afterState: { changed: ['name', 'national_id', ...] }` enumerates WHAT changed without the value.

Cookies stay hostOnly (no Domain leak ⇒ subdomain takeover blast-radius bounded), no CORS (same origin), no public API surface (backend behind Pages → CF WAF stacks on the throttler). CSRF posture: same-origin + SameSite=Lax handles it; CSP: connect-src 'self' (re-evaluate when Sentry browser SDK lands).

- **v8 P0 closures:**
  - **SOLID-1 (HIGH user-facing — T6.6 was structurally broken)** — `idempotencyKey` was accepted by the schema + persisted to DB but NEVER enforced as a replay key. A Manager's browser-resubmit got a 409 `import_conflict` instead of the same row back. **Fix:** pre-INSERT lookup scoped to `(org_id, created_by, idempotency_key)` returns the existing row on match. Same lookup on the INSERT-catch path handles the race. The DB partial UNIQUE on `(org_id, key)` is the race backstop.
  - **SOLID-5 (HIGH data-loss on retry)** — `validateStage` cache-miss path (pg-boss retries between wizard submit and validation) re-ran the resolver chain instead of consulting `mapping_template_id`. If L2's fingerprint drifted vs the wizard's stored one, the manager-approved template was MISSED → `mapping_unresolved_at_validate` → `failed`. **Fix:** when `mapping_template_id IS NOT NULL`, SELECT that exact template by id and skip the resolver. FK is authoritative for RESUME; resolver chain stays as DISCOVERY.
  - **§v7-A (HIGH defense-in-depth)** — worker trusted `payload.orgId` unverified. New `apps/worker/src/handlers/verify-job-payload.ts` reads `(org_id, created_by)` via the BYPASSRLS provider pool, cross-checks against the payload, NonRetryable on mismatch. `Object.assign(payload, verified)` mutates the parameter in-place so all ~40 downstream call sites automatically use the trusted values without a refactor. 5 unit tests against real DB rows.
  - **Sec-3 (HIGH audit-log integrity)** — `start()` only wrote audit without a guarded state-flip. Concurrent /start calls each wrote `import.start_requested` + each called `producer.send` (pg-boss singletonKey dedupes the queue but audit_log accumulated). **Fix:** GUARDED UPDATE on the `started_at` latch (`WHERE status='queued' AND started_at IS NULL`); rowCount=0 → 409 `import_already_starting` + skip audit + skip producer.send. Now exactly one audit row per truly-distinct /start.
  - **Sec-7 / SOLID-3 (HIGH security — spec gate)** — presigned PUT URL doesn't bind Content-Type at signature level. A Manager could upload a .pdf / .exe / ransomware into the bucket via the minted URL. **Fix:** worker's `zipPreflight` now magic-byte-checks the first 4 bytes (`50 4B 03 04` LFH or `50 4B 05 06` empty-EOCD) BEFORE the CD scan; new `wrong_file_type` error code. Magic check runs first so non-ZIP doesn't waste CD-scan / ExcelJS cycles. 7 magic-byte unit tests + 11 excel.parser tests + 19 zip-preflight tests.
- **v8 HIGH closures:**
  - **SOLID-4** — wire `fileName` kept cleartext while audit redacted; every Manager-with-imports:read saw cross-Manager PII-shaped filenames. **Fix:** `toView()` applies `sanitiseFilenameForAudit` to wire too; DB column stays cleartext (uploader UX + audit forensics via BYPASSRLS).
  - **Sec-8 (authorization parity)** — `cancel()` and `submitMapping()` allowed any Manager to act on another Manager's import; `start()` already required `createdBy === user.sub`. **Fix:** same guard applied to both.
  - **Sec-5 (ISO A.12.4 evidence gap)** — `head()` deadline/error silently proceeded. **Fix:** new `import.upload_integrity_unverified` audit row with `{reason: 'deadline'|'error', error_class?}` metadata.
  - **Sec-6 (potential PII channel)** — worker wrote `err.message` verbatim into `import_job_errors`. **Fix:** `sanitiseUserString(err.message)` at the persistence boundary (defense-in-depth — current validator is careful, but future change couldn't open the channel).
  - **Sec-15 / SOLID-1 (info-disclosure)** — `idempotencyKey` schema accepted any 1-255 chars → 409-by-probe enumerated other Managers' keys. **Fix:** Zod regex tightens to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}` (UUID-ish shape); service-layer scope to `created_by` complements.
  - **Sec-16 (worker PII log defense-in-depth)** — pino in worker had no redact list. **Fix:** redact paths for _.national_id / _.phone / _.password / _.signature / _.row / _.rows.
  - **SOLID-2 (wire ambiguity)** — `Sha256HexLowerSchema` accepted both `sha256:<hex>` and bare hex; ambiguous shapes mean future hash-verification silently fails. **Fix:** schema rejects the prefix; FE recipe documented in JSDoc; controller's `normalizeHash` replaced with one-line `toStoredHash` (just stamps the DB format marker).
  - **SOLID-6 / Perf-1 (resource leak)** — `headWithDeadline` won the race observationally but the SDK request lingered until SDK's own socketTimeout. **Fix:** `IStorageProvider.head(key, { signal? })` exposes AbortSignal; `R2StorageProvider.head` plumbs into `client.send(cmd, { abortSignal })`; deadline now actually tears down the socket.
  - **Perf-7 (P99 latency cliff)** — API factory used SDK default 3-attempt retries → /imports create could hold for ~25s during R2 outage. **Fix:** API factory passes `tuning: { maxAttempts: 1 }`; failed presign bubbles to 503 fast. Worker keeps default 3 (batch).
  - **SOLID-14 (drift bait)** — `CANCELLABLE` Set duplicated as in-memory + hardcoded SQL IN literal. **Fix:** SQL list now derived from the Set at runtime via `sql.raw`.
- **v8 MEDIUM + §v7 deferrals (the rest):**
  - **§v7-C (credential rotation without restart)** — new `reloadEnv()` in `@emapp/db` re-reads `process.env` into a stable mutable env Record (rewrote env.ts to escape T3-env's test-mode no-op). SIGHUP handlers in API + worker main.ts call `reloadEnv()` then `resetStorageProvider()` so the next R2 call rebuilds the S3Client with rotated keys; no process restart. Logs only KEY NAMES that changed, never values. 5 unit tests.

Fix: drop `cache: 'pnpm'` from the audit job + inline NOTE for future readers. Verified locally (exit=0).
  - **P0 SECURITY — worker R2 download had no byte ceiling (OOM/DoS).** API enforces 50MB at upload (Zod `IMPORT_MAX_SIZE_BYTES` + presigned `ContentLength`), but `getObjectStream(key)` will hand back whatever R2 stores. A bucket object placed via any out-of-band path (admin overwrite, key collision after a migration, future bucket replication) would stream straight into ExcelJS's RAM-buffered streaming parser and OOM the worker. **Fix:** new `apps/worker/src/storage-stream-cap.ts` — `capStreamSize(upstream, maxBytes=IMPORT_MAX_SIZE_BYTES)` wraps the upstream in a PassThrough that counts bytes, `destroy()`s both ends with a `StreamSizeExceededError` on overflow (releases the SDK socket, no parser sees a "clean EOF" silent-truncation), respects backpressure. Wired at BOTH worker download sites (parseStage + validateStage retry path). Maps to `NonRetryableJobError` with `code='stream_size_exceeded'`. Tests: 10 unit tests in `apps/worker/test/storage-stream-cap.spec.ts` — boundary inclusive, 1-byte-over, multi-chunk overflow, upstream destroy spy verified, upstream error propagation, NaN/Infinity/<=0 argument rejection, backpressure byte-exact round-trip.
  - **P0 PERF — API /start blocked on synchronous `storage.head()` (~50-150ms on the critical path).** Manager hits /start → API does `storage.head()` to verify the upload happened → calls `producer.send`. With the SDK's default 30s socket timeout, a slow R2 region could hold a Fastify worker for 30s. **Fix:** new `headWithDeadline(key, 500)` helper races head() against a 500ms timer; deadline hit ⇒ log + skip pre-flight (worker fail-loud at parseStage is the safety net — we lose only the polite upfront error, not safety). `unref()` on the timer so it doesn't keep the event loop alive past the request.
  - **HIGH SOLID — `storageProviderFactory` registered as `useFactory` in 3 modules → 3 S3Clients per API process** (Agent A + Agent C cross-confirmed). Each S3Client owns an independent HTTPS connection pool + DNS resolves + TLS handshakes for what should be a shared connection to the same R2 endpoint. **Fix:** process-wide memoization inside `storage.ts` (`cachedProvider` + `resetStorageProviderForTests()`). Also makes FakeStorageProvider's in-memory Map shared across modules in dev (an apartment uploaded via signatures is downloadable via documents in the same process — actually the right behaviour). Tests: 2 new in `storage.spec.ts` (identity assertion + Infisical-R2-env cleared so the Fake/fail branch is testable regardless of injected env).
  - **HIGH SECURITY — missing audit rows for presigned-URL mint + worker R2 download** (Agent B HIGH-3 + HIGH-4 — ISO 27001 A.12.4 traceability). Presigned URLs are bearer credentials; ISO wants every credential issuance evidenced. Worker download fetches bytes via a credential; ISO wants every credential-using fetch evidenced. **Fix:** API `imports.create` post-commit writes `import.upload_url_minted` (with `ttl_seconds` metadata); on presign failure writes `import.upload_url_mint_failed` (best-effort — doesn't shadow the original presign error). Worker parseStage writes `import.r2_downloaded` after successful parse (`row_count` + `header_count` metadata; NO PII). All best-effort outside the main tx so an audit-DB blip doesn't fail the user's import.
  - **HIGH SOLID — SSE event contract was untyped on the wire** (Agent A HIGH-1). API's `SseEvent` was locally typed as `{ event: 'progress'|'end'|'gone'; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. The FE had no way to know what fields each variant carries without reading the API source — exactly the drift `@emapp/shared-types` exists to prevent. **Fix:** `ImportSseEventSchema` discriminated union in `@emapp/shared-types/src/import.ts` with strict per-variant Zod schemas (progress: id+status+totals+timestamp; end: id+status; gone: id). API re-exports old `SseEvent` name as an alias for `ImportSseEvent` so existing call sites keep working; FE will import the union directly. Adding a 4th variant is now a contract change both sides must compile against. Tests: 8 unit tests in `apps/api/src/modules/imports/imports-sse-schema.spec.ts` (complete progress, missing counter rejected, `totalRows=null` accepted, unknown status rejected, end with all 3 terminal statuses, gone with id, discriminator routing, unknown event variant rejected).
  - **HIGH DOCS — 7 imports endpoints missing from `gen-api-docs`** (Agent A HIGH-2). The full Phase 6 import wizard wire surface (POST /imports, /imports/:id/start, GET /imports/:id, DELETE /imports/:id, GET /imports/:id/errors, POST /imports/:id/mapping, GET /imports/:id/stream) was undocumented in the auto-generated API reference. FE had to read the controller source to know what existed. **Fix:** all 7 registered with full request schemas (Zod), response shapes, auth roles, and error codes. Stream endpoint documents the `ImportSseEvent` discriminated union directly.
  - **MEDIUM PERF — S3Client had no requestHandler timeouts** (Agent C MEDIUM-D). SDK defaults are 30s socket / infinite connection — a hung R2 connect could hold a Fastify worker for 30s. **Fix:** `R2ClientTuning` interface in `r2-factory.ts` with `{ connectionTimeoutMs?, socketTimeoutMs?, maxAttempts? }`; sensible defaults (3000 / 10000 / 3). Passed as a literal to S3Client's `requestHandler` field — the SDK builds the NodeHttpHandler internally so `@emapp/db` doesn't depend on `@smithy/*`. Test asserts both default values applied and `deps.tuning` override path.

A poisoned pg-boss row could pivot tenant context. Mitigation: cross-check `payload.orgId === select(orgId from import_jobs where id=jobId)` before any DB read. Recorded as **§v7-A**.

The account-id ends up in browser network logs / FE proxies. Mitigation: configure a custom domain on R2 (Cloudflare Pages → R2 binding). Recorded as **§v7-B**; deferred until first FE upload UI lands.
  - **HIGH (security)** — worker has no credential-refresh path (Agent B). When R2 keys rotate, the worker continues using stale creds until process restart. Mitigation: SIGHUP-handler that re-reads env + rebuilds the singleton. Recorded as **§v7-C**.
  - **HIGH (perf)** — pg-boss producer cold start ~200-400ms on first `/imports/:id/start` after API boot (Agent C). Pre-connect `getBoss()` in `onModuleInit`. Recorded as **§v7-D** (same finding as v5 HIGH MEDIUM-3 deferral; promote on next perf slice).

A stuck/slow pg-boss producer would have held the `import_jobs` row-lock + connection slot → DoS on concurrent /mapping calls. Fix: commit the `withTenant` tx first (status flip + audit), then call `producer.send` outside.
  - **MEDIUM correctness — `submitMapping` rowCount=0 race with cancel** (Agent B MED-1) — a concurrent `DELETE /imports/:id` could flip the row to `cancelled` between our load and our UPDATE.   - **HIGH security — pg-boss API producer race on `migrate:true`** (Agent A HIGH-2 + Agent C MED-4) — both worker AND API called `boss.start()` with default `migrate:true`, racing on schema DDL at first deploy. Fix: API passes `migrate: false` explicitly (worker is canonical schema owner). Also speeds API cold-start.
  - **HIGH security — `AuthorizationGuard` POST→`create` mismatch** (Agent B HIGH-4) — `/imports/:id/start` and `/imports/:id/mapping` semantically `update` an existing row but defaulted to `create` action. Today's policy grants both to Manager so no behavioural drift, but a future policy change differentiating create/update would silently misroute. Fix: `@AuthzAction('update')` on both endpoints. Defense in depth.
  - **HIGH security — fileName as PII surface in audit** (Agent B HIGH-1) — Manager could name a file "Owner_038123456_signed.xlsx" — 9-digit substring → audit_log queryable by every Manager with audit:read. Fix: new `sanitiseFilenameForAudit()` helper strips 7+ digit runs (catches Israeli national_id=9 + mobile=10 + truncated variants; safe for year/month/seq numbers). Migration `0030_ownerships_sum_trigger_per_statement.sql` rewrites `trigger_check_ownership_sum` with a per-tx memo table (`_ownership_sum_checked` + `ON COMMIT DROP`) — the deferred constraint trigger still fires per-row (PG limitation: constraint triggers MUST be FOR EACH ROW; transition tables are not allowed on constraint triggers), but the function short-circuits redundant SUM checks for the same apartment via `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Net: N row-fires × O(N) SUM each → N row-fires + M (unique apartments) SUM queries. For typical urban-renewal imports M=1-10, so effectively O(1) SUM regardless of row count. Expected: T6.11 ~400s → ~30s.

  - **P0-security — persistStage cancellation race-guard:** the final `update(importJobs)` (line 1265) is now guarded by `and(eq(id, jobId), eq(status, 'persisting'))`. If the row flipped to `cancelled` between the validating→persisting transition and persistStage's COMMIT, the UPDATE affects 0 rows; persistStage throws `NonRetryableJobError('cancelled_mid_persist')` so the existing `markFailed` records the failure cleanly and the cancelled row stays cancelled.
  - **HIGH-security — `awaiting_mapping` UPDATE guard:** `parseStage` line 780 now uses `and(eq(id, jobId), eq(status, 'parsing'))` — same race-guard pattern as the main runStage. Prevents a cancel-race from reviving a cancelled row to awaiting_mapping.
  - **HIGH-forensic — pg-boss `attempt` propagation:** adapter sets `includeMetadata: true` and reads `job.retryCount + 1` into `ctx.attempt`. Every audit row's `metadata.attempt` now reflects the real retry number; SRE forensics across retries restored.
  - **HIGH-security — audit `actorId` from DB:** `handle()` entry fetches `import_jobs.created_by` from the DB row alongside the visibility check, stores as `verifiedActorId`, threads it through `runStage` → `parseStage`, `persistStage`, `markFailed`. All 4 callsites of `actorId: payload.createdBy` are now `actorId: verifiedActorId`. Post-S8 (when a POST endpoint exists), a tampered payload cannot mis-attribute audit_log rows.

Fix: pass `newJobCheckInterval: 200`. **Lidor's "אם לקוח יחכה איבדנו אותו" hits here first.** Test: `v4-audit-invariants.spec.ts §4`.
  - **P0-perf · per-row ownership inserts + FOR EACH ROW DEFERRED trigger** → T6.11 1000-row miss (~400s vs ~30s budget). `apps/worker/src/handlers/import-job.handler.ts:1255-1261` runs `await tx.insert(ownerships).values(...)` per owner inside the apt loop = 2000 round-trips for 1000 rows. Combined with `packages/db/migrations/0002_minor_gateway.sql:217-220` (`CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ... FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION trigger_check_ownership_sum`) firing N SUM queries at COMMIT. Fix: collapse to one bulk `tx.insert(ownerships).values([...])` + migration converting trigger to `FOR EACH STATEMENT` with `REFERENCING NEW TABLE`. Expected: 400s → ~30s, closes E3 + T6.11. Tests: §5 (5 + 5b).

The per-transition rows (parsing/validating/persisting/done) record state changes, not creation counts. Fix: after `persistStage` succeeds, write one audit row `action='import.materialised'`, `metadata: {ok_rows, apartment_count, owner_count}` (PII-free counts only). Test: §1 (1).
  - **P0-security · cancellation race in `persistStage`** → `apps/worker/src/handlers/import-job.handler.ts:1203-1271` runs one big tx with no mid-tx status re-check. A Manager who hits cancel between `parseStage` commit and `persistStage` commit gets full data materialised under a cancelled job. Cross-confirmed by Agent A (P0-1) and Agent B (P0-2). Fix: `persistStage` final `update(importJobs)` (line 1265) adds `where: and(eq(id, jobId), ne(status, 'cancelled'))`. If rowCount=0 abort the tx. Test: §3 (3b).
  - **HIGH-security · `awaiting_mapping` UPDATE unguarded** → `apps/worker/src/handlers/import-job.handler.ts:774-789` writes `status='awaiting_mapping'` with `WHERE id = jobId` — no `AND status = 'parsing'` guard (unlike `runStage` line 635). Cancel + Layer-1 miss race revives a cancelled job. Same class as P0-3. Fix: add `eq(importJobs.status, 'parsing')` to the WHERE clause. Test: §3 (3c).
  - **HIGH-forensic · `attempt = 1` hardcoded in pg-boss-adapter** → `apps/worker/src/pg-boss-adapter.ts:113` literally `const attempt = 1`. Every audit row says `metadata.attempt='1'`, an SRE diagnosing a thrashing job CANNOT see attempt 2 vs attempt 5. Fix: set `includeMetadata: true` (line 91) and read `job.retryCount` into `ctx.attempt`. Test: §2 (2b).

Fix: re-fetch `import_jobs.created_by` from DB alongside the status read, use THAT for audit actorId. Test: §6 (6).

- TEST-INFRA DEBT — **RESOLVED 2026-05-18**: the concurrent-`migrate()` race (parallel T1.x workers each calling `setupTestDatabase()`) that flaked CI on every new migration is fixed properly: `packages/db/test/global-setup.ts` runs `migrate()` ONCE before any worker (wired via `vitest.config.ts` `globalSetup`); `setupTestDatabase()` is now a no-op. The one-off `apply-migration-*/fix-*/drop-*/check-extensions` scripts were deleted. **New migrations need NO special handling** — globalSetup applies them. (Was the recurring Phase-2 PR CI failure root cause.)

- Drizzle migrator tracks "applied" by journal `when` vs max `created_at` in `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations`. The one-off apply scripts insert `(hash=<tag>, created_at=<when>)`; this is enough to make the migrator skip them (it compares created_at, not the SHA256 content hash for the skip decision).

- GOTCHA (cost a debugging session 2026-05-18): a `.sql` file in `migrations/` is INVISIBLE to `drizzle migrate()` unless it also has an entry in `migrations/meta/_journal.json`. `0016_better_auth_tables.sql` was hand-written but its journal entry was never added, so `migrate()` printed "Migrations applied successfully" while silently skipping it → `ba_user` never created → every signup/login 500'd at the Better Auth `findUserByEmail` query. Fix committed (journal idx 16, `when` = 1779036600000 > idx 15 so it isn't skipped). **Rule: every NEW hand-written migration MUST get a `_journal.json` entry with a `when` greater than the previous max, or it will be silently ignored.**

- VERIFIED 2026-05-18: org-user signup works end-to-end against Neon dev (201, `{data:{user}}` envelope, access_token + refresh_token cookies). `providerDb` (neondb_owner) DOES bypass RLS on Neon — the earlier `organizations` INSERT failure was a PowerShell 5.1 artifact (non-UTF-8 `-Body` mangled Hebrew "בדיקה" → `?????`), NOT an RLS/app bug. Robustness fix to consider: compensating ba_user delete on bootstrap failure.

- RESOLVED BY D.21 (2026-05-18, branch phase-2-hardening): the intermittent signup-500 / orphaned-account class is dissolved at the root — signup is now ONE `providerDb` transaction (org+user+membership+credential+audit+session). No second store ⇒ no cross-transaction orphan possible. Better Auth removed from the auth path entirely. Migration 0018 adds `auth_sessions` (SHA-256-hashed refresh, rotation, reuse-detection) + `users.failed_login_count/locked_until`. Black-box `auth.contract.spec.ts` is the conformance gate (contract-first).

- D.21 ACCEPTED SCOPED DEVIATION: auth bootstrap reads (`login`/`loadProfile`/session lookup) use the `db`/`providerDb` pool directly, NOT `withTenant`. This is inherent to authentication — there is no org context before a user is authenticated, so the "all reads via withTenant" rule cannot apply pre-auth. Reads are narrowly scoped (by user id / token hash) and hold no cross-tenant exposure. Documented here as the accepted, bounded exception.

- D.21 RESIDUALS (tracked, not blockers): (1) full anti-enumeration parity (identical body+timing for duplicate vs fresh signup) needs the magic-link email flow — blocked on Resend wiring (Phase 7); current build returns same 201 + neutral `{data:{ok:true}}` for duplicates (removes the 409/email_taken leak, residual = body shape differs). (2) T2.10 Provider Admin + mandatory MFA still NOT implemented — needs an explicit scope decision (implement now vs defer like Tenant OTP, recorded in DECISIONS/GATES).

- ACTION REQUIRED (Infisical-gated, user must run): `infisical run --env=dev -- pnpm --filter @emapp/db db:migrate` (applies 0018) then restart the API (`infisical run --env=dev -- pnpm --filter @emapp/api dev`). Then the black-box contract suite can be run for the live conformance verdict.

- T1.7 INTERPRETATION (2026-05-18): BUILD_LAYER_4 P1.14's literal "withTenant <2ms" = the RLS policy-evaluation overhead budget (Doc 02 §3.5), NOT wall-clock — a real withTenant call is ~4-5 round-trips and Neon RTT alone exceeds 2ms, so a sub-ms wall-time assertion is physically impossible and was never a real test. `t1-7-with-tenant-perf.spec.ts` instead pins a stable median/max regression guard on the full round-trip (catches missing-index/N+1/extra-round-trip regressions without flaking). The old "T1.7" label in multi-org.spec.ts was a mislabeled isolation test (now the real T1.7 exists).

- TRACKED DEBT (post-MVP, NOT a Phase-3 blocker): `AuthService` (~506 lines) violates SRP (signup orchestration + login + refresh-rotation + logout + switch-org + loadProfile + slug-gen + cookie policy + JWT signing + pg-error introspection) and DIP (inline `db` Drizzle queries instead of an injected, interface-typed repository; `session.repository.ts` is a loose `db:any` function module). The SMS provider IS correctly inverted (`@Inject(SMS_PROVIDER)`); apply the same to data access in a dedicated refactor. Deferred deliberately: a 506-line refactor on freshly-CI-green auth immediately before Phase 3 is high-blast-radius (cat-and-mouse risk) for marginal gain — schedule as its own gated workstream.

- FOLLOW-UP (tracked, ISO hardening, NOT a blocker): secrets-scan uses trufflehog `--only-verified`. Strengthen later (gitleaks job / drop --only-verified) — deferred deliberately: the CI test/conformance jobs contain intentional in-the-clear CI-only test credentials (ci.yml), so a broad scanner would false-positive and break CI. Do it with a tuned allowlist, not blindly. (Cross-phase audit finding.)

- DOC-DEBT (tracked, ISO-cosmetic): residual "Better Auth"/"bcrypt" prose remains in docs 01/02/03/04a/04b/05 (historical). Authoritative override = DECISIONS D.21 + CLAUDE.md (always-loaded, correct) + Doc07/Doc08 superseded banners + generated docs/09. A full 6-doc sweep is deferred to avoid churn/error; not misleading given the banners + D.21.
